key_insight: Continual learning can intensify demographic unfairness in deepfake detection, and preserving accuracy alone does not ensure equitable outcomes.
engineering_relevance: Engineers deploying evolving deepfake detectors should monitor demographic fairness alongside accuracy and forgetting; this study does not directly address solid mechanics.
method: Train detectors progressively on a chronological sequence of deepfake generation methods.
Track four fairness dimensions across demographic groups and intersections.
Compare rehearsal-, prompt-, and regularization-based continual learning methods.
evidence_signal: Evaluation across 11 real-world deepfake generation methods found that accuracy degradation typically exacerbated unfairness, while fairness improvements remained scarce over time.
watch_item: Underrepresentation alone did not explain inequitable forgetting; the suggested role of representation learning requires further investigation.
paper_title: Time to Fake It: Continual Machine Learning Intensifies Unfairness in Deepfake Detection
